In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cytochrome aa(3) is essential for symbiosis but that the cytochrome oxidase activity of the bacteroids is not.
the Tn5-induced cytoplasmic membrane mutations of B. japonicum strains LO501 and LO505 affect the electron transport system in both free-living cultures cells and symbiotic bacteroids.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Tn5-induced cytoplasmic membrane cytochrome mutants LO501 and LO505 are defective in the oxidation of TMPD and NADH and have a reduced amount of cytochromes b, c, and aa3 in free-living cells but are not defective in bacteroid cytochromes.
the symbiotic function of cytochromes is not the same as that in the free-living bacterium, and the cytochrome c aa3 oxidase is essential for symbiosis.
the Tn5 insertion in LO505 disrupts the heme biosynthetic pathway, and the insertion in LO501 disrupts a branch of the electron-transport system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cytochrome content and electron transport activity of cultured cells are not good indicators of the cytochrome composition of root nodule bacteriods.
the Tn5-induced mutants are useful tools for the study of the role of cytochromes in the free-living growth of B. japonicum as well as in the symbiotic growth of bacteroids.
the cytochrome c and aa3 genes in B. japonicum are not essential for N2 fixation, but they are essential for the synthesis of leghemoglobins.
